newsitem.title: MONGOLIA: Mongolian tugrik falls after presidential polls.
newsitem.headline: Mongolian tugrik falls after presidential polls.

text.p: The Mongolian tugrik slipped to 787.76 to the U.S. dollar on Monday after opposition candidate Natsagiin Bagabandi won Sunday's presidential elections, Mongolia's central bank said.
The rate was 778 tugriks to the dollar on Friday, the Bank of Mongolia said.
That compared with 693.51 tugriks against the U.S. currency on December 31, 1996.
Commercial banks in the Mongolian capital were buying U.S. dollars for 750-790 tugriks, while the market rate in the streets on Monday offered 800-807 tugriks for the greenback.

Preliminary results showed Bagabandi, 47, a Soviet-educated technocrat and candidate of the opposition Mongolian People's Revolutionary Party (MPRP), had won a decisive 60.79 percent of the vote in Sunday's polls, far exceeding opinion poll forecasts.

Speaking after casting his vote on Sunday, Bagabandi said if elected president he would cooperate with all parties, but also pledged to try to slow down the government's radical reforms that that have created widespread economic dislocation.
